content.title: Lakers vs. Rockets: Prediction, How to Watch for Free (3/16/26)
content.text: The Los Angeles Lakers (42–25) visit the Houston Rockets (41–25) tonight at the Toyota Center in the first of a two-game set between two teams locked in a tight Western Conference race as the regular season enters its final stretch. Just a half-game separates the third-place Lakers and the fourth-place Rockets. Los Angeles has surged into the top three on a five-game winning streak, capitalizing on recent struggles by several conference rivals. On Saturday, the Lakers defeated the Denver Nuggets 127–125 in overtime on a Luka Doncic game-winning shot with less than a second remaining. The drama began earlier, when Austin Reaves intentionally missed a free throw, grabbed his own rebound, and scored with 1.9 seconds left in regulation to force overtime. Reaves finished with 32 points, while Doncic recorded a 30-point, 11-rebound, 13-assist triple-double. Marcus Smart added 21 points, and LeBron James contributed 17. Houston, meanwhile, narrowly beat the struggling New Orleans Pelicans 107–105 on Friday night, with Kevin Durant hitting a go-ahead basket in the final 10 seconds. With Alperen Sengun still sidelined, Durant led the Rockets with 32 points. Amen Thompson added a 23-point, 12-rebound double-double along with eight assists, and Reed Sheppard scored 18 points off the bench. The Lakers and Rockets run it back on Wednesday in Houston. The Rockets are 2–2 over their last four games and have struggled against elite Western Conference opponents during that stretch, including lopsided losses to both the San Antonio Spurs and Denver Nuggets. Houston will battle at home, but expect Los Angeles to prevail in a tight finish. Prediction: Los Angeles Lakers 120, Houston Rockets 115 Injury Report Los Angeles Lakers Maxi Kleber — Out (Back) Houston Rockets Alperen Sengun — Out (Back) Jae’Sean Tate — Out (Knee) Steven Adams — OFS (Ankle) Fred VanVleet — Out (Knee) How to Watch Lakers vs. Rockets Tip-off for today’s Lakers-Rockets game is set for 9:30 PM Eastern / 8:30 PM Central / 6:30 PM Pacific at the Toyota Center in Houston. Local fans can catch the game on Spectrum SportsNet and Space City Home Network. The game will air nationally on NBC Sports Network and stream on Peacock.
